note: The dated change log on /bitcoin-lenders (JM's rulings 2026-10-01: a section above the cards plus card badges and per-card history; seeded with the changes the 2026-09-30 research found with exact, sourced dates; every monthly re-read logged even when nothing changed). Newest entries may go anywhere: the index (lenderLogIndex.js) sorts by date. kind: 'check' (a re-read of the cards; give read and changed counts) | 'page' (a card added or removed) | 'lender' (something the lender changed). type, for kind 'lender' or 'page': 'rate' | 'terms' | 'availability' | 'launch' | 'added' | 'removed' | 'exit' (kind 'lender': the lender changed something) | 'updated' (kind 'page': the card brought into line with the lender’s own pages at a re-read, whether the lender changed or the card was incomplete; no claim about when the lender changed it). lender: the card id in lenders.json. source: the lender's own page for the change. changes (optional, kind 'lender' or 'page'): [{field, was}] with field one of rate, open, call, liq, trig, coins, terms, minimum, where, track; the card highlights those lines for 14 days, showing 'was …' when `was` is short. lenders (optional, kind 'check'): the card ids the check covered; absent means every card. Procedure: MONTHLY_REFRESH_CHECKLIST §7.6.

entries.text: Monthly re-read: all twenty cards checked line by line against each lender’s own pages (Ledn’s state list and Coinbase’s help pages in a desktop browser); twelve cards changed. Strike’s volatility-proof loan reached Washington and its credit line fell to 11.25%; APX moved to 1–5 year terms; Firefish published default interest of 15%; Aave raised how much you can borrow against bitcoin to 81%, with liquidation at 85%. Unchanged: Ledn, Figure, SALT, both Kraken products, Nexo, Unchained and Better.
Strike’s volatility-proof loan is now offered in Washington; it is still not offered in CT, DE, MD, NY, PR, SC or TX.

changes.was: not in CT, DE, MD, NY, PR, SC, TX or WA

entries.text: Strike’s credit line rate now reads 11.25% (it was 13.25%; Strike resets it each quarter from the prime rate), and the card adds Strike’s higher minimums for monthly-interest loans in Iowa, Oklahoma and South Carolina.

APX rewrote its loans page: terms are now 1 to 5 years with interest billed monthly, and repaying early costs three months’ interest on the amount repaid; the 5-year credit line and the instalment and deferred options are no longer listed.
Firefish’s liquidation FAQ now spells out default: if you don’t repay at maturity, default interest of 15% a year runs from the due date and a liquidation premium of about 5% is taken.
Aave’s Ethereum market now lets you borrow up to 81% of WBTC or cbBTC and liquidates at 85% (the card had 73% and 78%); rates refreshed to 5 November (USDT 4.61%, USDC 5.63%).
Arch’s site footer no longer lists Hawaii among excluded states for individuals; the card also corrects the eligibility article’s count to 43 states, DC and Puerto Rico.
Debifi’s offer book refreshed to 5 November (8.5–14.25%); its FAQ adds 0.3% to the opening fee for a second year, and a $500 minimum for card loans.
Hodl Hodl’s offer book refreshed to 5 November: 9.5–12.5% a year.
Morpho’s Base cbBTC/USDC market refreshed to 5 November: 5.7% (6-hour average), $177 million available.
The card adds Coinbase’s 1% fee on fixed-rate loans and its optional loan protection, which tops up collateral from your balance at a loan-to-value you set.
The card adds Lava’s optional Liquidation Protection, which tops up collateral from your Lava bitcoin balance past a threshold.
Milo’s pages re-read: the product page still says 7–9% and $275,000, its 2026 guide 6.5–8.5% and $200,000 to $25 million; the calculator’s default quote is now 7.625% on $400,000.
The “servers are currently down” banner Cadena showed on 30 September was gone by 5 October; the track record line now says so.
Three cards re-read in full ahead of the monthly check (Strike, Ledn, Nexo); two updated. Nexo’s US terms still don’t say whether it may lend out or re-pledge collateral, so its card is unchanged.

Card updated from Strike’s help-centre tables: rates for paying interest monthly (7.49–10.50%) added beside the pay-at-the-end rates (8.75–11.25%); the volatility-proof loan costs 2.95 points more (was “about 3”); states from Strike’s own table (no personal loans in Delaware, Hawaii or Maryland; the volatility-proof loan is offered in California, and not in CT, DE, MD, NY, PR, SC, TX or WA); a personal loan starts at $10,000 in most states (was “$5,000 in some”).

States now from Ledn’s own eligibility tool: not available in California, Connecticut, Hawaii, Nevada, North Dakota, South Dakota, Tennessee, Washington or DC, and available in New York. The card had relied on other lenders’ comparison charts.
Added to the page: Cadena Bitcoin, the only Discreet Log Contract lender here. Twenty cards.
Page published. All nineteen cards read from each lender’s own pages, every figure dated.
Kraken Borrow launched in the US: buying power on Kraken, not a cash loan you can withdraw.
APX cut its liquidation fee to 0% and moved to partial liquidation: it now sells only enough bitcoin to bring the loan back to 85%.
Hodl Hodl Lend’s new terms bar US citizens, residents and anyone in the US, reversing its 2020 opening to US users.
Nexo returned to the US through Bakkt, three years after leaving.
